teams.heading: Mesake Doge sent off as Fiji Latui lose 62-12 to Ireland XV
teams.body: Fiji Latui's discipline unravelled at Virgin Media Park on Friday night: four first-half yellow cards, three of them inside five minutes, left the second-string side down to 12 men for a spell. Mesake Doge's first yellow was for a high tackle on Todd Lawlor; 30 seconds after returning he collected a 20-minute red for collapsing a third consecutive scrum. Pita Lesivoukionoilau's interception try had given the visitors their only lead in the seventh minute, and Jope Naseara added a breakaway score.

lead.why: Both NEW items fail the Fiji test (#1 is Italy's post-match reaction and #2 is Italy's late prop change), so the freshest unrun story about a Fiji side leads.

teams.heading: Lewis Moody faces the haka alongside England before 37-12 All Blacks rout
teams.body: The former England captain, diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year, stood between Maro Itoje and Ellis Genge as England faced the challenge, then watched from the stands as they won 37-12 on Saturday. He had presented the shirts on Friday night, and Steve Borthwick told BBC Radio 5 Live that Moody "spoke unbelievably in the way he put his message across and it really resonated with the players." Every England player wore boots carrying the logo of his Front Up to MND campaign.

lead.why: Moody joining the haka line is the most talked-about England moment from Saturday, and the scoreline itself has already run.

teams.heading: France's 45-17 bonus-point win over Argentina books Twickenham final against Springboks
teams.body: Seven tries, five after the break, earned France the attacking bonus point in Saturday's 45-17 win over Argentina at the Stade de France, edging them past England to top the Europe pool on 25 points. Fabien Galthié's side now face South Africa in the Nations Championship final at Twickenham, a rematch of their 21-19 win in Saint-Denis earlier this month. Rugbyrama's ratings flagged a worry: Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang went off just after the hour with an apparent muscle injury, though replacement Emilien Gailleton scored with his first ball.

lead.why: France's bonus-point win topped the pool and set up a final rematch with the Springboks, the biggest new France story.

teams.heading: Ireland will face former defence coach Les Kiss in fifth-place play-off
teams.body: After Saturday's 20-17 win over South Africa, Andy Farrell's side finished third in the Northern Hemisphere ladder. The42 reports that this sets up a meeting with Australia at Twickenham in the Nations Championship finals weekend. Kiss, Ireland's ex-defence coach and a former Ulster boss, succeeded Joe Schmidt as Wallabies head coach earlier this year. His side sealed third in the Southern Hemisphere table by edging Wales 29-26 on Saturday. France and South Africa contest the final.

lead.why: Ireland's next opponent is confirmed, with a former Ireland coach in the other dugout.

teams.heading: Simone Ferrari's late injury forces Italy front-row reshuffle before Fiji defeat
teams.body: Italy lost 16-21 to Fiji in Udine on Saturday without Simone Ferrari, ruled out about an hour before kickoff with an injury to his left upper limb, OnRugby reported. Marco Riccioni was promoted from the bench to start at tighthead, with Ion Neculai taking the No. 18 shirt. Ferrari will be assessed in the coming days to gauge his recovery time, with the Fiji rematch ahead. Despite the reshuffle, captain Giacomo Nicotera said Italy's scrum had done good work and was becoming a weapon.

lead.why: A fresh injury to a senior Italy forward, with a forced late change to the starting XV, is the newest hard news about the team.

teams.heading: Townsend hopes Matt Fagerson injury is not serious before Twickenham finals weekend
teams.body: Saturday's 67-5 rout of Japan at Murrayfield came with one back-row worry for Gregor Townsend, who singled out his starting No. 8 afterwards: "Matt Fagerson went through a lot of work and hopefully his injury isn't serious." The 11 tries left Scotland fourth in the northern hemisphere table but with a vastly improved points difference, and the head coach said his side still don't know what their week will look like before finals weekend at Twickenham.

lead.why: Its new fact is Matt Fagerson's injury, the one development since the Japan rout we already ran.

teams.heading: Dewi Lake's TMO plea ignored after Tupou's alleged strike on Alex Mann
teams.body: Saturday's 26-29 defeat to Australia has left viewers fuming at the officials. After Wales won a scrum penalty, footage appeared to show Wallabies prop Taniela Tupou aim a swinging forearm at Alex Mann's midriff. Captain Dewi Lake told referee Luc Ramos that Australia's No. 3 had punched Wales' No. 6 and urged a TMO review, WalesOnline reports, but neither the referee nor the TMO acted. Tupou scored the opening try shortly afterwards and could yet be cited.

lead.why: It is the newest and most talked-about Wales story: Lake's captaincy plea was ignored over an alleged strike on Mann before Australia's opening try.

teams.heading: Pumas crushed 45-17 by France after Mayco Vivas red card in Paris
teams.body: Argentina's 45-17 defeat at the Stade de France unravelled after the hour. Hollie Davidson's yellow for Mayco Vivas was upgraded to red, and Julián Montoya's later yellow left the Pumas 13 against 15. The damage had started early: Santiago Chocobares withdrew hours before kick-off, and Bautista Delguy and Boris Wenger went off without returning. Justo Piccardo's try from inside centre and Tomás Albornoz's boot put the visitors 10-7 up. Pablo Matera's interception was the only second-half reply. Scotland await in a battle for seventh.

lead.why: It is the only new event about the Pumas: a heavy defeat shaped by a red card and injuries.

teams.heading: Wallabies' Cardiff win over Wales sets up Ireland fifth-place play-off
teams.body: The 29-26 result sealed third in the Southern Hemisphere table of the Nations Championship, so Les Kiss' side meet Andy Farrell's Ireland, third in the Northern Hemisphere ladder, for fifth place at Twickenham, The42 reports. The win also ended a run of four defeats, per the Guardian. Len Ikitau's 64th-minute try and a late Carter Gordon penalty left Wales needing a try they never found. Their final attack broke down with a forward pass, SA Rugby Magazine reports.

lead.why: Fresh, corroborated news about Australia: the Wales win decided the Wallabies' finals-weekend opponent.

teams.heading: Japan's 67-5 Murrayfield defeat leaves southern hemisphere fifth place exposed to Fiji
teams.body: Saturday's 67-5 defeat to Scotland — 11 tries conceded, after a 78-15 hammering by England the week before — may cost Eddie Jones' side more than pride. OnRugby reckoned it could knock Japan out of fifth place among the southern hemisphere sides should Fiji beat Italy with a bonus point and a decent margin. Rugby Asia 247's preview had already tipped the Brave Blossoms to finish bottom or second-bottom of their pool, potentially setting up a finals-weekend rematch with Wales or a meeting with Italy.

lead.why: The Matsunaga try and sin-bins have already run; OnRugby's report adds a new angle: what the rout could cost Japan in the standings.

teams.heading: All Blacks miss Nations Championship final and face England again for third
teams.body: South Africa pipped New Zealand to top spot in the southern-hemisphere table, and France's win over Argentina took them past England, the Guardian reports. That sends the All Blacks straight back into a third-place final against the side that beat them 37-12 at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. It was the widest margin New Zealand have ever lost by to northern-hemisphere opposition. Maro Itoje already has the rematch in view: "We don’t want this to be our ceiling, we don’t want this to be as good as we get."

lead.why: The defeat has already run; the new development is that it decided New Zealand's finishing route and set up an immediate rematch with England.

teams.heading: Grant Williams says 'stupid penalties' must go before Twickenham final against France
teams.body: The Springboks will face France in the inaugural Nations Championship final at Twickenham. Saturday's 20-17 defeat in Dublin still earned a losing bonus point, enough to edge New Zealand for top spot in the southern table, Planet Rugby reports. Williams, the scrumhalf-cum-wing, wants all 23 to take a hard look at themselves and named discipline as the problem: "They got into our half with stupid penalties and they converted." Les Bleus won 21-19 in Paris last week and routed Argentina 45-17 to reach the final.

lead.why: A fresh Springbok reaction that names the problem to fix before the final rematch with France.
